in_text_mentions: Clinical examination revealed hemorrhagic crusts associated with atrophic and varioliform scars on the cheeks and nasal tip (Figure 1A). There was no mucosal involvement (oral, conjunctival, corneal, or genital).

The dermoscopic image reveals whitish scar-like areas scattered with rosettes and small, rounded follicular plugs (Figure 1B). Unlike leishmaniasis, where facial follicular plugs often appear as peripheral teardrop-shaped structures, this pattern differs. It also contrasts with discoid lupus erythematosus, where follicular plugs are typically found at the periphery of scarring areas, indicating active disease. Additionally, the linear and dotted vascular pattern observed here differs from the short vessels seen in leishmaniasis and the arborizing vessels characteristic of discoid lupus. Also,

The papulovesicular lesions or bullae most often develop an erythematous base and are initially tense, followed by progressive necrosis that leads to healing with a varioliform scar (Figure 2). In addition, a mixture of hyper- and hypopigmented lesions results in a polymorphous skin presentation. The differential diagnosis for HV at this stage includes erythropoietic and hepatic porphyrias, which can be excluded by checking the level of porphyrins in the blood and urine, as well as phototoxic reactions, a vesiculobullous form of polymorphous light eruption, and actinic prurigo

different lesions. In early stages of HV, characteristic histologic features in the skin include intraepidermal spongiotic vesiculation, varying degrees of lymphocytic infiltrate in the upper dermis (Figure 2) and areas of keratinocyte necrosis [7,10]. A histologic hallmark of HV, suggested by Iwatsuki et al., is a dense perivascular lymphocytic infiltration with reticulated degeneration of the epidermis [9]. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient clinical photo from a disease-focused HV article. Panel A shows an ulcerated, crusted nasal bridge (necrotic crusts) and a crusted lower lip (cheilitis/facial edema), recognized HV manifestations. The article frames the case as 'presenting as benign photodermatoses', so the presentation is atypical. B: Real patient clinical photo. Caption and in-text attribute the plantar eczematous lesions to the HV case ('plantar lesions demonstrated an eczematous morphology'). Eczematous morphology is not a vocabulary HV finding, so it is captured as a proposed finding; attribution rests on the disease-focused article title plus the captioned manifestation. Nonspecific morphology, hence lower confidence.
